definition: The practice of teams working together effectively while geographically distributed, using digital tools for communication and coordination.
extendedDefinition: Remote collaboration is the practice of teams working together effectively across locations using digital tools for communication, coordination, and shared work. Effective remote collaboration depends on reducing friction: synchronous tools like video and chat cover live interaction, while asynchronous tools such as shared documents, recorded meetings, and threaded updates carry the workload across time zones. The quality of collaboration tooling directly affects distributed teams' speed, because every untracked decision or unreachable document creates delays that compound daily. Buyers should evaluate how tools handle handoffs, notifications, and search, since information must be findable long after it was created. Remote collaboration also changes management practices, favoring written clarity, scheduled rhythm, and documented processes. When comparing products, teams should test real multi-site workflows including mixed modes, rather than evaluating each tool in isolation.
